changes.before: Cisco Talos, the threat research arm of Cisco, reports in a blog published on 8 Oct 2026 that across 84 malware samples from four families collected between January 2025 and July 2026, authors embedded plain-language text, such as instructions to ignore or refuse to analyse the file, to steer the AI tools that analysts use to triage suspicious files (a trick known as prompt injection). In Talos's own tests on five local AI models, simply telling the model to ignore the file worked almost universally, while more elaborate versions had little effect or made the models more suspicious; Talos says conventional detection is unaffected and calls the trend 'interesting, but not alarming', though it shows attackers expect AI inside defenders' tools.
changes.after: Cisco Talos, the threat research arm of Cisco, reports in a blog published on 8 Oct 2026 that across 84 malware samples from four families collected between January 2025 and July 2026, authors embedded plain-language text, such as instructions to ignore or refuse to analyse the file, to steer the AI tools that analysts use to triage suspicious files (a trick known as prompt injection). In Talos's own tests on five local AI models, the plainest trick, an instruction to ignore the file, nearly always worked, while more elaborate versions did little or raised the models' suspicion; Talos says ordinary detection is unaffected and calls the trend 'interesting, but not alarming', though it shows attackers expect AI inside defenders' tools.
changes.reason: Copying: second sentence closely followed quote_evidence; reworded.
